x: On returning to England in 1919 he was talked into training again by Jimmy Belchamber. Although he did not get back the pace that had formerly made him so formidable he soon became a very sound and reliable team man at seven and ten miles.

Among the members joining during the years just preceeding the war was Jimmy Belchamber who after a season or two became an outstanding member of the long distance walking team in the London to Brighton Walk.
He had run at most distances, was a boxer of no small repute; and on the persuasion of Jimmy Belchamber, had become a distance walker of outstanding merit.

Coming to 1921 we find that Jimmy Belchamber finished second in the Brighton and Back race in 20:53:35 to become No. 64. Jimmy was a Past President of the Club and served in many offices, for instance for many years he was Hon.

The late Jimmy Belchamber did much for the Club in the years between the two World Wars, particularly with regard towards the walkers. He was no mean performer himself over the longer distances and was also one of the Club's Hon.
